Professional private pick-up service and check in Hotel — Rest and acclimatization to local climate and environment
Hongya Cave Night View — A real-life "Spirited Away" scene. 11-story traditional stilt houses on the cliff, glowing with warm yellow lights after dark. Lights: 6:00 PM — 11:00 PM. Best photos from Qiansimen Bridge or Grand Theater riverbank.
Qiansimen Bridge Night View — A bright red cable-stayed bridge over the Jialing River. Lights up like a red dragon, perfectly matching Hongya Cave. Lights: 8:00—10:30 PM (summer); 7:30—9:30 PM (winter). Walk on the bridge for close-up views.
Day 02
Tue, Nov 2, 2027
Chongqing - Old Town Charm of Yuzhong
Landmarks, Ancient Alleys, Local Food & Night Views
▾
🗺Jiefangbei Pedestrian Street → Bayi Food Street → Mountain City Trail → Shibati → Lunch & Break → Yangtze River Cableway → Hongyadong Folk Custom Area → Qiansimen Bridge
✈ TransportPrivate car
🏨 HotelLocal 4-star level hotel
🍽 MealsBreakfast
Jiefangbei Pedestrian Street — A city landmark of Chongqing. Visit the Victory Monument and stroll around the bustling downtown area to experience the urban vibe of the mountain city.
Bayi Food Street — A well-known food street with a great variety of local snacks. Taste spicy noodles, sweet glutinous rice balls and ice jelly at your leisure.
Mountain City Trail — A traditional trail featuring old residences, ancient trees and riverside plank roads. Wander downhill to feel the authentic local life of old Chongqing effortlessly.
Shibati — Once the vital passage connecting the upper and lower parts of the old city. It features layered stone steps and a mix of old and new architecture, presenting the history of Chongqing.
Yangtze River Cableway — Known as the "air bus" of Chongqing. Cross the Yangtze River by cable car and enjoy panoramic views of the two rivers and unique mountain city landscapes. Time is reserved for queuing and photos.
Hongyadong Folk Custom Area — Explore the clustered stilt houses built along the hillside. Visit cultural and creative shops, try local delicacies and wait for the lights to turn on.
Qiansimen Bridge — Walk onto the bridge, the best spot to take full photos of Hongyadong. Admire the stunning river scenery and night views before heading back to the hotel.
Day 03
Wed, Nov 3, 2027
Chongqing - Internet-famous Spots & Ancient Towns
Unique Landscapes & Traditional Alleys
▾
🗺Liziba Light Rail Station → Eling No.2 Factory → Lunch & Break → Ciqikou Ancient Town → Longmenhao & Xiahaoli
✈ TransportPrivate car
🏨 HotelLocal 4-star level hotel
🍽 MealsBreakfast
Liziba Light Rail Station — A famous scenic wonder of Chongqing. Head to the viewing platform to take photos of the light rail running through a residential building.
Eling No.2 Factory — A cultural and creative park renovated from old factory buildings. It features industrial-style architecture and graffiti. Enjoy city and river views on the viewing platforms.
Ciqikou Ancient Town — A time-honored riverside ancient town. Wander along stone streets, try local specialties like fried dough twists, and watch folk performances such as Sichuan opera face-changing.
Longmenhao & Xiahaoli — Original old streets on the south bank. Well-preserved old houses, Republic of China architecture and ancient trees create a quiet atmosphere, showing the original style of old Chongqing.

Xi'an Arrival

Warm welcome by your local guide and driver.
Comfortable transfer to your hotel (quasi‑4 star).
Night view of Xi'an Bell Tower — Appreciate splendid ancient tower night scenery and feel classic ancient city charm.
Night view of Xi'an Drum Tower — Admire elegant ancient architecture and enjoy charming downtown night views.

Wander over to the Bell and Drum Towers after dark—they’ve stood guard over Xi’an’s heart since the Ming dynasty, and tonight their timber frames glow softly against the indigo sky, lit just enough to reveal centuries of carved eaves and upturned corners. The square between them buzzes gently: street vendors roll out sesame cakes still warm from the griddle, calligraphers ink quick characters on rice paper, and the occasional burst of *qin* music drifts from an open courtyard café. You’ll pass under the Drum Tower’s massive wooden beams—still hung with the original 24 drums used to mark time for the city—and pause at the Bell Tower’s marble base, where the 14th-century bronze bell rests silent but palpably present. It’s not about spectacle here; it’s the quiet hum of history folding into everyday life, one lantern-lit step at a time.

Day 06
Sat, Nov 6, 2027
Xi'an - Xiaonanmen Morning Market → Shaanxi History Museum → Giant Wild Goose Pagoda → Tang Paradise Ever-Bright City
▾
🗺Xiaonanmen Morning Market (breakfast) → 0.5h → Shaanxi History Museum → 0.2h → Giant Wild Goose Pagoda → 0.1h → Tang Paradise Ever-Bright City→Return to hotel
✈ TransportPrivate car
🏨 HotelLocal 4-star level hotel
🍽 MealsBreakfast
Xiaonanmen Morning Market (1 hour) — Feel local daily life, taste traditional breakfast and experience authentic Xi’an morning customs.
Shaanxi History Museum (2 hours) — Appreciate precious cultural relics and learn about long-standing history of Shaanxi region.
Giant Wild Goose Pagoda and Square (1.5 hours) — Visit the ancient pagoda and relax in the square to enjoy elegant Tang-style scenery.
Tang Paradise Ever-Bright City (2.5 hours) — Stroll through grand Tang-style streets, enjoy splendid night views and feel prosperous ancient charm.

Start your day at Xiaonanmen Morning Market, where Xi’an’s rhythm is set by steaming *roujiamo* stalls, hand-pulled noodle vendors, and elders practicing tai chi beside the old city wall—this isn’t a tourist show, but a lived-in slice of local life just outside the South Gate. From there, walk ten minutes to the Shaanxi History Museum: its bronze-and-terracotta galleries hold over 370,000 artefacts, including Tang dynasty gold hairpins and Han dynasty jade burial suits—arrive early to skip the queue and linger in the quiet, climate-controlled halls. A short taxi ride brings you to the Giant Wild Goose Pagoda, built in 652 CE to house sutras brought back from India; climb its seven storeys for views over the surrounding park and the faint echo of temple bells on the breeze. End the day at Tang Paradise Ever-Bright City—a thoughtful reconstruction of Chang’an’s Tang-era imperial gardens—not as a theme park, but as a gently lit, canal-lined stroll past pavilions, ink-wash style lanterns, and open-air performances of court music that feel quietly reverent, not theatrical.

Day 07
Sun, Nov 7, 2027
Xi'an - Terracotta Army → Song of Everlasting Sorrow→Muslim Quarter Food Tour
Terracotta Army → Song of Everlasting Sorrow
▾
🗺Hotel breakfast → Terracotta Army → drive 1 hour → Song of Everlasting Sorrow→Muslim Quarter Food Tour→Return to hotel
✈ TransportPrivate car
🏨 HotelLocal 4-star level hotel
🍽 MealsBreakfast
Terracotta Army Museum (2.5 hours) — World-famous ancient imperial mausoleum relics. Admire vivid clay warrior formations and discover glorious Qin Dynasty history.
Song of Everlasting Sorrow Show (2 hours) — Classic live outdoor performance staged at Huaqing Palace. With natural mountain scenery, it depicts touching ancient royal love stories.
Muslim Quarter Food Tour (1.5 hours) — amous local food street. Taste authentic Shaanxi snacks and experience authentic local folk customs.

Standing before the Terracotta Army in Pit 1—where over 6,000 life-sized warriors stand in precise, silent formation—you’ll notice the subtle individuality in each face: a furrowed brow here, a slight smile there, all hand-sculpted over 2,200 years ago for Emperor Qin Shi Huang’s afterlife. A short drive away, the *Song of Everlasting Sorrow* show unfolds at Huaqing Palace, a Tang-dynasty hot spring resort where the tragic romance of Emperor Xuanzong and Yang Guifei is told through choreography, water screens, and live orchestration against the misty Lishan Mountain backdrop—best experienced on a clear autumn evening when the air carries the scent of pine and the music lingers long after the final bow. It’s not about spectacle for spectacle’s sake; it’s the quiet weight of history, felt first in the cool, earthy hush of the pits, then in the lyrical ache of a story that’s been sung in Xi’an for centuries.

Standing before the Terracotta Army in Pit 1—where over 6,000 life-sized warriors stand in precise military formation—you’ll notice the subtle differences in facial features, hairstyles, and even armour details, each hand-sculpted over 2,200 years ago for Emperor Qin Shi Huang’s afterlife guard. A short drive to Huaqing Hot Springs sets the scene for the *Song of Everlasting Sorrow*, where you’ll walk the same willow-lined pathways and pavilions where Emperor Xuanzong and Yang Guifei once strolled—and where Bai Juyi later composed his famous Tang dynasty poem mourning their tragic love. The contrast is quietly powerful: one site speaks of imperial power frozen in clay; the other, of human vulnerability echoing across centuries in poetry and steam rising from ancient thermal pools. You’ll have time to sit with both—not as relics, but as layered, breathing parts of China’s living memory.
